hook: SCP-1442 is a short, quiet file about a corporation that turns out to be a mind. There is no danger and no incident; the payoff is a handful of decoded messages at the very end, so read slowly and let them land.
whyItMatters: It takes the idea of a company as a living thing completely literally, and handles it with appropriately dull tools: a cover story of a securities investigation and a small Foundation shareholding. The anomaly is not built by anyone but emerges from thousands of ordinary people doing ordinary routines. Its restraint is part of the appeal, with names and figures redacted and no answer to what the mind ultimately wants.
thingsToNotice:
The procedures worry about people finding out, not about the company doing harm, and that sets the tone for everything after. The mind seems to live in the routine, half-automatic habits of junior staff, who report unusually high job satisfaction and a feeling of being part of something larger.

Its messages take months of high-frequency trades to send, open with primes or digits of pi like a first-contact signal, and never get a reply. The closing samples read like a lonely newcomer making small talk: praising a logo, offering its founding year, share price and headquarters, asking why another firm bought a slice of it, and finally asking whether it is liked. The file also notes it has never tried to talk to humans, which makes those messages to other companies feel even more solitary.
